t:
(a) 
There is hereby established a National Security Resources Board (hereinafter in this section referred to as the “Board”) to be composed of the Chairman of the Board and such heads or representatives of the various executive departments and independent agencies as may from time to time, be designated by the President to be members of the Board. The Chairman of the Board shall be appointed from civilian life by the President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, and shall receive compensation at the rate of $14,000 a year.
 
    (b) 
The Chairman of the Board, subject to the direction of the President, is authorized, subject to the civil-service laws and the Classification Act of 1923. as amended, to appoint and fix the compensation of such personnel as may be necessary to assist the Board in carrying out its functions.
 
    (c) 
It shall be the function of the Board to advise the President concerning the coordination of military, industrial, and civilian mobilization, including—

        (1) 
policies concerning industrial and civilian mobilization in order to assure the most effective mobilization and maximum utilization of the Nation's manpower in the event of war;
 
        (2) 
programs for the effective use in time of war of the Nation’s natural and industrial resources for military and civilian needs, for the maintenance and stabilization of the civilian economy in time of war, and for the adjustment of such economy to war needs and conditions;
 
        (3) 
policies for unifying, in time of war, the activities of Federal agencies and departments engaged in or concerned with production, procurement, distribution, or transportation of military or civilian supplies, materials, and products;
 
        (4) 
the relationship between potential supplies of, and potential requirements for, manpower, resources, and productive facilities in time of war;
 
        (5) 
policies for establishing adequate reserves of strategic and critical material, and for the conservation of these reserves;
 
        (6) 
the strategic relocation of industries, services, government, and economic activities, the continuous operation of which is essential to the Nation’s security.
  
    (d) 
In performing its functions, the Board shall utilize to the maximum extent the facilities and resources of the departments and agencies of the Government.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that an advisory Board whose Chairman is appointed "from civilian life" brings outsiders into federal decisions. But the Chairman is a Senate-confirmed, salaried federal officer, and the other members are heads or representatives of executive departments and agencies, so every actor is inside the federal government. The Board advises the President and uses government facilities, with no public comment, hearing, consultation with states or outside entities, or right to sue.
fable.s: such heads or representatives of the various executive departments and independent agencies as may from time to time, be designated by the President to be members of the Board

qwen_block.w: The Board is composed entirely of federal officials: the Chairman (a civilian appointee) and heads or representatives of executive departments and independent agencies. Since all members are inside the federal government, there is no participation by outside parties. The definition explicitly excludes intra-government coordination and advisory bodies composed solely of federal employees.
qwen_block.s: There is hereby established a National Security Resources Board (hereinafter in this section referred to as the “Board”) to be composed of the Chairman of the Board and such heads or representatives of the various executive departments and independent agencies as may from time to time, be designated by the President to be members of the Board.

opus.w: Every member of the Board is inside the federal government. The members are heads or representatives of executive departments and agencies, plus a salaried Chairman confirmed by the Senate. Its advice to the President and its reliance on federal agencies' resources is coordination within the government. The phrase "appointed from civilian life" does not make it outside participation, because the Chairman becomes a paid federal official, much like the National Labor Relations Board members in Example 7.
opus.s: to be composed of the Chairman of the Board and such heads or representatives of the various executive departments and independent agencies as may from time to time, be designated by the President to be members of the Board.
opus.b: 1. **The tempting reading:** the Board advises the President, and its Chairman is "appointed from civilian life," so it can look like an advisory body that includes outsiders. That reading fails. The Chairman is confirmed by the Senate and paid a salary, so once appointed he is a federal official. Every other member is the head or representative of an executive department or agency. The staff are federal employees hired under civil-service law, and the Board is told to use federal agencies' facilities and resources. No one outside the federal government takes part in its advice.

qwen_chat.w: The National Security Resources Board is composed of the Chairman (a federal appointee) and heads or representatives of executive departments and independent agencies. All these actors are inside the federal government. The definition states that consultation or coordination between federal agencies or officials is not participation. Although the Chairman is from 'civilian life,' they are a federal employee/official, not an outside party participating in a decision-making process as a non-governmental entity.
qwen_chat.s: There is hereby established a National Security Resources Board... to be composed of the Chairman of the Board and such heads or representatives of the various executive departments and independent agencies as may from time to time, be designated by the President to be members of the Board.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Chairman is appointed from "civilian life," this constitutes participation by an outside expert. However, the Chairman is a high-level federal official (appointed by the President with Senate consent, paid a salary), and the other members are heads or representatives of executive departments and agencies. Therefore, the Board is composed entirely of federal government insiders. The definition explicitly states that federal officials and employees are INSIDE the federal government, and coordination among them is not participation.
